summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: algorithm analysis (big-O, Omega, Theta, recurrences, divide and conquer including Karatsuba, schoolbook multiplication), discrete mathematics (induction, modular arithmetic, gcd and coprimality, primes, permutations, binary representation and XOR), a first linear algebra course (matrices, inverses, Gaussian elimination, vectors and bases), polynomials and complex numbers with roots of unity, and basic Turing machines with tapes. They have met the FFT at most as an algorithm for polynomial multiplication, and they have not studied multitape complexity in depth, finite fields beyond the bit field, abstract algebra, tensor products, or numerical error analysis.

known.name: Omega, Theta and little-o notation
known.gloss: Companion asymptotic notations to big-O: Ω(f) is an eventual lower bound, Θ(f) is both upper and lower bound, and o(f) means the ratio to f tends to zero.

known.name: Logarithms and floor/ceiling
known.gloss: Base-2 logarithms (the number of bits needed to write an integer) and the floor and ceiling functions that round a real number down or up to an integer.

known.name: Binary representation and two's complement
known.gloss: Integers written as strings of bits, with negative integers stored in a fixed-width signed two's-complement word.

known.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: Long multiplication of n-digit numbers costs O(n^2) digit operations, and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer trick lowers this to O(n^{log_2 3}).

known.name: Divisibility, gcd and coprimality
known.gloss: The greatest common divisor of two integers, coprime meaning gcd 1, and the extended Euclidean algorithm that finds the Bezout coefficients and hence modular inverses.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers taken modulo q, where a ≡ b (mod q) means q divides a − b, and an element has an inverse modulo q exactly when it is coprime to q.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: Integers greater than 1 divisible only by 1 and themselves, with unique factorization into primes; deterministic primality testing by trial division is available for small numbers.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A bijection of a finite index set to itself, i.e. a reordering of an array, which can be composed and inverted.

known.name: Matrices and matrix inverses
known.gloss: Rectangular arrays of numbers acting on vectors by multiplication, with the identity, invertible matrices, diagonal and triangular matrices, and their products and inverses.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Row reduction of a matrix by elementary row operations to solve linear systems, find rank, or invert a matrix.

known.name: Vectors, bases and dimension
known.gloss: Standard first-course linear algebra: linear combinations, independence, bases, dimension, dot products and orthogonality.

known.name: Bitwise XOR and arithmetic over F2
known.gloss: XOR of bits is addition modulo 2; bit vectors then form vectors over the two-element field, and the Hamming weight counts the ones in a bit string.

known.name: Exponentials of imaginary numbers and geometric series
known.gloss: Euler's formula e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ puts roots of unity on the unit circle, complex numbers have modulus and conjugate, and geometric series Σ rᵏ have closed forms, including the vanishing sum of all q-th roots of unity.

known.name: Triangle inequality and sup norm
known.gloss: The norm of a sum is at most the sum of norms, and the maximum of the absolute values of the entries of an array is a norm, so errors can be bounded and added.

known.name: Induction and recurrences
known.gloss: Proofs by induction, telescoping sums, and solving divide-and-conquer recurrences such as T(n) ≤ a T(n/b) + O(n).

known.name: Stacks and sorting
known.gloss: A last-in first-out stack as used by recursion, comparison and radix sorting of records, and linear scans over an array.

known.name: Word RAM and unit-cost model
known.gloss: A machine model with random access to memory in which arithmetic on words of O(log n) bits takes one step, in contrast to the Turing machine where data movement costs time.

known.name: Fixed-point and two's-complement arithmetic precision
known.gloss: Numbers stored with a fixed number of fractional bits are rounded with bounded error, and integers in base b are added by propagating carries digit by digit.
